Distribution. Japan (Hokkaido I.). Comparison. The new species may easily be recognized by its robust ovipositor with two distinct dorsal subapical teeth (Fig. 5), antennal flagellum with 23 – 25 flagellomeres (Fig. 6), and simple tarsal claws. Similar ovipositor is known in the European A. boops (Gravenhorst), but in this species the ovipositor is much shorter (sheath about as long as first tergite), flagellum with 14 – 15 flagellomeres, and tarsal claws distinctly pectinate.
